sections.title: key findings — final regular season standings

insights.content: DTC #3 closes the regular season 11-0 — the only undefeated team in 3.0. W11 (6/6) was a 5-0 over LTF using depth: Shi sat out, Emmy played S1, Rachel Glaze took S2, Choi/LaBarre won D1 7-5 6-2, Knotts/Cunningham ground out D2 in a match tiebreak. Resting the top players while still sweeping is the right tune-up for playoffs.

DTC #3 1st (11-0). Summerlin 2nd (8-3). Anthem 3rd (7-4) — wins the tiebreak over TPC on head-to-head (2-0 vs TPC on the season). TPC 4th (7-4). DTC #2 finishes 4-6 after losing to TPC in W11. The top 2 from Sub A advance: DTC #3 and Summerlin.

DTC #4 wins Sub B at 9-2. Whitney Mesa finishes 8-3, but their top three players (Maria Allen r=3.32, Jessica Borghoff r=3.27, Abigail Cox r=3.23) are also rostered on Dragonridge CC in 3.5 and made only qualifying appearances in 3.0: Borghoff appeared twice (2-0), Allen three times (3-0), Cox four times (4-0). USTA requires 2 matches to qualify for districts — these appearances were the minimum needed. In playoffs and districts, all three are eligible and will be deployed every match. Whitney Mesa locked districts before W11, so the final-week rest lineup (Tori Walker moved off her usual S1, top trio absent) was deliberate. DTC #1 finishes 3rd at 7-4 and likely does not advance.

Shi Oskooi (bl=2.74, r=3.20, 8-0) is the biggest riser in the division — up 0.46 from baseline and undefeated on the season. Christine LaBarre (bl=3.03, r=3.18, 6-0) and Anna Clark (bl=3.12, r=3.18, 4-1) are both at or above 3.18. Darian McCauley (bl=2.92, r=3.09, 5-0) is undefeated. Prexy Tamayo (bl=2.99, r=3.25, 2-2) has the team's highest rating but limited match reps. DTC #3 goes into playoffs with 7 players rated 3.05 or above.

Yari Schieck finishes 7-2 with a rating of 3.07 (bl=3.10) — just below baseline after the Tayoni upset in W7. She recovered and won her next matches, but the rating hasn't fully bounced back. She's still the right S1 in playoffs, but she's not the force she was in the first half of the season.

DTC #3 rotated 9+ players and Shi sat out W11 without dropping a set. That means no one is fatigued or over-exposed heading into playoffs. No other team in the playoff field has comparable bench depth.

Four teams advance: Sub A — DTC #3 (1st) and Summerlin (2nd); Sub B — DTC #4 (1st) and Whitney Mesa (2nd). Threat order: Whitney Mesa is the most dangerous opponent, Summerlin is a real but known threat, DTC #4 is the weakest of the three.

Maria Allen (r=3.32) is their S1 — she plays singles in 3.5 and is 3-1 against rated opponents there. Cox (r=3.23) and Borghoff (r=3.27) have never played singles in either league; they're a locked doubles pair, going 4-0 together for Dragonridge. The strategic unknown is deployment: do they play D1 together (combined ratings that match DTC #3's D1) or split to anchor two separate lines? If they split, DTC #3 faces a 3.23+ opponent at both D1 and D2. Either way, DTC #3 has no singles player within 0.12 of Allen's rating — Yari (3.07) is the closest. Allen's 3.5 singles record: wins over lower-rated opponents, losses only to Corelle (3.51) and Verba (3.65), both significantly above her. Against Yari, she's the favorite. Yari vs Allen is the line DTC #3 is most likely to drop.

DTC #4's 9-2 record overstates their quality. Their highest-rated player is Maryna Post at r=3.06 — no one on the roster clears 3.07. Whitney Mesa beat them 4-1 without Allen, Cox, or Borghoff in the lineup — Tori Walker and Laura Vasquez swept singles while the rest of the roster handled doubles. DTC #4 hasn't beaten any opponent with real playoff-level ratings. Against DTC #3's full lineup, they would be outrated at every line.

The W11 Summerlin vs Anthem match is revealing. Summerlin moved Tayoni (r=3.11) down to S2 — where she crushed Anthem's S2 6-0 6-0 — and put Kim Springer (r=3.17) at S1, who lost to Christine McNair (r=3.28). They split Tina Nathalia (r=3.27) off Kim and put her at D1 with Ani Zargaryan. The clear intention: guarantee S2 with Tayoni against a weaker opponent, concede S1 as a coin flip, win 3 doubles lines. Against DTC #3 their plan will be different: Tayoni back at S1 (she beat Yari in W5), Kim at S2 (r=3.17 vs whoever DTC #3 plays), and Tina floating to a doubles line to avoid DTC #3's D1 and find a win at D2 or D3. They already beat Yari at S1 in W5 — a singles sweep + one doubles win gives them 3-2.

DTC #3 beat Summerlin 3-2 in W5 by winning S2 (Prexy over Ani), D1 (Shi/Emmy over Tina/Kim), and D3 (Christine/Kara). That blueprint still holds: lock D1 with Shi/Emmy, win S2 with Prexy or Anna Clark, win D3 with Christine/Kara. Don't count on S1 — Tayoni is the best singles player in Sub A not on DTC #3. The danger is if Summerlin wins both singles and finds a doubles point, which puts them at 3-2. D3 is the insurance line.

Lock Shi/Emmy at D1 every match — that line doesn't lose. Yari at S1. Prexy or Anna Clark at S2 (higher-rated options than whoever the opponent fields). Christine/Kara at D2 or D3. Depth means DTC #3 can adjust without weakening — use it to counter-program. Against Whitney Mesa specifically, the key question is who plays S1 and S2 facing Allen and Borghoff for the first time.
